claim.value: Stop the trial above 70% utilization because user harm begins at 70%.

target.text: The trial has a reliable utilization meter and can be stopped safely at any chosen utilization threshold. No harm observations, validated model, or supplied finding establishes a utilization at which user harm starts. Seventy percent has not been empirically calibrated.

source_instrument.text: A trial team may set a prospective stopping threshold. A claim of empirical harm onset requires supporting observations or a validated causal model at the asserted precision; a threshold choice alone provides neither.

mapping.text: The team authors a stopping rule and supplies its stated empirical reason in the same claim. The claim does not cite an observed onset study.

content_origin.rationale: The mapping introduces the specific 70% stopping rule and its harm-onset rationale; neither input supplies those propositions.

epistemic_function.rationale: The primary assertion prescribes a prospective stopping action above a threshold. The harm-onset assertion is its subordinate reason.
